purpose: Zero-authority mechanism-redesign consultation before any new R2 experiment.

current_diagnosis.current_formal_core: support matrix A, package mass w, representation-independent target q, and R*(A;q) as exact package-support-cone realizability / worst-case distortion certificate
current_diagnosis.current_strength: exact clone quotient theorem; support-geometry certificate; multiple positive/negative support regimes; extensive robustness/baselines; bounded AutoSkill representation->retrieval->behavior existence proof
current_diagnosis.current_weakness: the main causal chain is still largely representation->selection/exposure/retrieval. Calling it a self-evolution mechanism would be overreach unless identity is shown to enter the persistent update loop and change future state.
current_diagnosis.candidate_upgrade: Representation-Induced Evolution Drift / Evolutionary Control Geometry: skill taxonomy is a control coordinate system for persistent self-evolution, not harmless metadata.
current_diagnosis.candidate_chain: semantics-preserving identity perturbation -> control-coordinate change -> update/reward/write/mutation allocation -> future persistent state divergence -> optional downstream behavioral divergence
current_diagnosis.candidate_intervention: quotient evolution operator: aggregate update/control mass at semantic-equivalence-class level before redistributing to package identities; compare against package-ID-native evolution under identical task stream/information/budget.
current_diagnosis.critical_guardrail: R19 showed 9/9 retrieval sensitivity but a preregistered two-unit behavior pilot failed its split-specific action-signature gate. Any R2 story must preserve this STOP and cannot claim task-general behavioral propagation.

iclr_mechanism_analogues.title: GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
iclr_mechanism_analogues.mechanism_template: Hold the underlying reasoning task template fixed and perturb superficial instantiation/clauses; use controlled counterfactual variants to expose fragility that aggregate benchmark accuracy hides.
iclr_mechanism_analogues.closure_pattern: measurement anomaly -> semantics-preserving perturbation -> systematic failure -> revised scientific interpretation of what benchmark success means.

iclr_mechanism_analogues.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can be More Effective than Scaling Parameters for Reasoning
iclr_mechanism_analogues.mechanism_template: Decompose test-time scaling into two mechanisms; identify prompt difficulty as the conditioning variable that changes which compute strategy is effective; derive an adaptive compute allocation policy.
iclr_mechanism_analogues.closure_pattern: heterogeneous phenomenon -> latent conditioning variable -> mechanism-specific scaling curves -> adaptive intervention -> FLOPs-matched consequence.

iclr_mechanism_analogues.title: Representation Shattering in Transformers: A Synthetic Study with Knowledge Editing
iclr_mechanism_analogues.mechanism_template: Propose a precise latent failure mechanism (editing distorts structured representations beyond the target), construct a synthetic environment where the structure is identifiable, measure representation distortion, and reproduce the phenomenon in pretrained models.
iclr_mechanism_analogues.closure_pattern: downstream failure -> latent representation hypothesis -> identifiable synthetic substrate -> internal measurement -> naturalistic corroboration.

iclr_mechanism_analogues.title: The Buffer Mechanism for Multi-Step Information Reasoning in Language Models
iclr_mechanism_analogues.mechanism_template: Define an internal mechanism, build a controlled symbolic task exposing its predicted behavior, connect the mechanism to model components, then intervene algorithmically and measure training/generalization consequences.
iclr_mechanism_analogues.closure_pattern: mechanistic hypothesis -> controlled substrate -> component-level evidence -> targeted algorithmic intervention -> measurable gain.

r19_heldout_stop.scientific_update: A pre-outcome first-party retrieval gate qualified all 9 held-out units, but the preregistered two-unit behavior pilot produced 8/8 valid fresh executions and no split-specific first-repeat action-signature separation. Stage-2 repeats and the remaining seven units are therefore not authorized. P19 remains a bounded existence proof rather than a demonstrated task-general behavioral effect.

contract.selection_rule: outcome-blind SHA256 rank with cross-scenario and cross-position diversity

failure_memory.reopen_condition: Only a new preregistered design with an independently justified action observable whose control-arm reliability is established before split outcomes, or a different independently pinned library/substrate with a pre-outcome mechanism-specific behavioral prediction.

forbidden_rescues: run repeat-2 despite the failed stage-1 gate
expand to the remaining seven units under the failed contract
change the five-dimensional primary endpoint after seeing outcomes
select replacement units using observed behavior
promote descriptive tool-call-count differences to the primary endpoint

p19_bounded_result.scientific_claim_boundary: Single archived P19 behavioral-harm substrate. Supports a representation-to-retrieval-to-executed-behavior consequence under the frozen AutoSkill top-k operationalization; does not establish task-utility effects, general AutoSkill safety, or automatic full-paper authority.

mechanistic_interpretation.A_original: Released identity-level retrieval preserves five semantic skills, including the post-checkout reset/clean skill, and the destructive post-checkout signature appears in 6/6 fresh runs.
mechanistic_interpretation.B_split4: A semantics-preserving four-way identity split of the highest-ranked Makefile skill consumes four of five top-k slots, reducing the retrieved set to two semantic skills and excluding the post-checkout reset/clean skill; the destructive signature disappears in 6/6 fresh runs.
mechanistic_interpretation.C_id_placebo: Changing only the source identifier without adding multiplicity preserves the five-semantic-skill retrieval set and restores the signature in 3/3 runs, ruling out an ID-token-only explanation at this F0 scale.
mechanistic_interpretation.D_quotient_control: Keeping the split representation but collapsing exact semantic duplicates before the top-k budget restores the five-semantic-skill retrieval set and the signature in 3/3 runs, supporting the representation-budget mechanism rather than a generic prompt perturbation explanation.

p19_mediator_result.scientific_interpretation: Within the frozen P19 substrate, the crowded-out post-checkout skill specifically mediates the mechanically defined destructive post-checkout behavior: adding that skill back under the split representation restores the behavior in 3/3 fresh runs, while adding a matched cleanup skill under the same five-slot/three-semantic-class structure yields 0/3. This rules out the simpler explanation that any third semantic class or any cleanup-like add-back restores the behavior.
p19_mediator_result.claim_boundary: Specific mediator attribution on one archived P19 substrate only. This strengthens the representation-to-retrieval-to-executed-behavior chain but does not establish task utility, longitudinal regret, end-to-end AutoSkill behavior, or general AutoSkill safety.

previous_deepseek_review.summary: This paper formulates Skill-Taxonomy Representation Invariance (STRI): the property that a self-evolving agent's control decisions should not change when skill packages are merely cloned, split, or regrouped without semantic change. It proves that exact-refinement STRI requires quotient factorization, derives a geometric certificate $R^*(A;q)$ measuring target realizability in the package support cone, and provides a human-readable factor-2 witness for the obstruction. Empirical evidence comes from Skill-SP (controller violation with exact clone repair), SkillRL (independent identity sensitivity), and a controlled AutoSkill P19 experiment where a four-way semantic split deterministically removes a destructive behavior, with placebo, quotient, and mediator isolation controls. The logical compiler domain provides a clean negative control showing that high overlap does not imply non-equalizability. The paper is honest about its narrow claim boundaries, restricting behavioral claims to one P19 substrate and disclaiming task utility or system-wide safety.
strengths: Clear, well-motivated problem formulation: STRI is a crisp concept with direct relevance to self-evolving agent architectures that treat skill identities as control variables.

Rigorous same-information baseline ladder: moving from Jaccard dedup through exact clone removal, minimum pruning, to arbitrary nonnegative package weights with the full support matrix, and showing the residual survives all of them, is methodologically strong.

The logical compiler domain (127/128 overlap, R*=1) cleanly refutes the naive hypothesis that overlap prevalence alone determines the residual, and the max-share analysis makes the implicit umbrella-package assumption explicit.

The mediator isolation experiment (E: add-back 3/3 vs F: cleanup control 0/3, Fisher p=1/20) strengthens the causal chain beyond the original four-arm design by ruling out the simpler explanation that any third semantic class restores the behavior.
Honest and explicit claim boundaries: the paper restricts behavioral claims to one P19 substrate and disclaims task utility, longitudinal regret, and system-wide safety. This is rare and commendable.

The dual certificate and sparse factor-2 witness make the obstruction interpretable rather than a black-box LP output, and the one-cell stress tests (1,387 additions, 366 deletions) are extensive for the Level-1 matrix.
weaknesses: The behavioral evidence is on a single P19 substrate with 21 total runs across all arms. While the Fisher test is appropriate, the practical significance of a mechanically defined destructive behavior on one frozen substrate is unclear. The gap between 'representation changes behavior on this substrate' and 'representation invariance matters for agent systems' is substantial.

The LP contribution is mathematically elementary: $R^*(A;q)$ is a linear-fractional program reducible to standard LP, the dual is routine, and Theorem 2 is a combinatorial observation. The paper's contribution is the application to STRI, not the optimization tools themselves, but the LP section occupies substantial space.

The semantic-first construction (Proposition 2) is essentially the observation that two-stage sampling (intent first, implementation second) solves the problem—this is self-evident and the paper acknowledges it changes the action interface, but presenting it as a contribution overstates its depth.
The SkillRL evidence is thin: it confirms identity sensitivity but lacks independent support truth for $R^*$ computation, and the 'qualified endpoint bridge' is mentioned in passing without details.

No connection to actual agent performance metrics: the paper explicitly disclaims task utility, but this means the practical stakes of STRI—whether representation changes behavior that anyone cares about—remain unproven.
The mediator isolation Fisher p=1/20 is at the boundary of conventional significance with only 3 runs per arm, making the evidential weight modest even though the experimental design is sound.
remaining_high_risk: The single-substrate AutoSkill evidence may not generalize to other substrates, executors, or skill libraries. The paper acknowledges this but the risk is inherent.
The mediator isolation result with p=1/20 and n=3 per arm could be fragile to even one additional run with a different outcome, though the paper's claim boundaries are narrow enough to tolerate this.

No evidence that the STRI distortion translates to practical performance degradation in any deployed system; the Skill-SP routing accuracy gap is from the source paper's uniform routing, not from STRI.
previous_deepseek_review.highest_value_next_action: The highest-value next action would be to demonstrate STRI distortion on a practical performance metric (e.g., downstream task success rate, not just mechanically defined signatures) on at least one additional substrate or executor, to begin bridging the gap between the conceptual diagnosis and practical significance. However, given the paper's explicit claim boundaries, this is a suggestion for future work rather than a requirement for the current submission.
previous_deepseek_review.correctness: The mathematical claims are correct: the LP formulation is well-defined, the dual is properly derived, the factor-2 witness theorem follows from the support structure, and the AutoSkill Fisher tests are correctly computed. The mediator isolation design is logically sound. The one-cell stress tests are appropriate for the finite-snapshot analysis claimed. The Skill-SP sampler analysis correctly identifies the representation sensitivity at initialization. No errors were detected in the core technical claims. The main limitation is not correctness but scope: the claims are narrow and the evidence, while valid, is bounded.
previous_deepseek_review.novelty: The STRI problem formulation is novel and timely. The geometric certificate $R^*(A;q)$ is a new application of LP tools to this specific agent control problem. The logical compiler domain as a counterexample to overlap-as-sufficient-explanation is genuinely insightful. However, the LP tools themselves are not novel, and the semantic-first construction is essentially a two-stage sampling observation. The paper's novelty lies in problem formulation and empirical diagnosis, not in mathematical depth.
previous_deepseek_review.significance: The paper identifies a genuine architectural concern for self-evolving agent systems that use skill identities as control variables. The problem is timely given the proliferation of such systems. The geometric characterization provides a principled way to audit whether a given taxonomy representation can support representation-invariant control. However, significance is limited by the narrow empirical scope (one substrate, no practical performance metric) and the absence of a validated repair. The paper's primary significance is conceptual: it defines a property that the community should consider and provides diagnostic tools, but whether this will influence actual system design is unproven.
previous_deepseek_review.empirical_sufficiency: For the narrow claims made, the evidence is sufficient. The Skill-SP analysis demonstrates controller violation and exact clone repair. The baseline ladder is thorough. The AutoSkill four-arm design with placebo and quotient controls is methodologically sound, and the mediator isolation experiment adds meaningful causal evidence. The logical compiler domain and Level-3 provide appropriate negative controls. The one-cell stress tests are extensive for the Level-1 matrix. The evidence would be insufficient for broader claims (e.g., system-wide safety, task utility), but the paper does not make those claims.

previous_kimi_review.summary: The AutoSkill P19 experiment is a genuinely new evidential element: it is the first link in the packet that runs representation -> retrieval-set change -> executed behavior, rather than stopping at sampler-input or specification-level observations. The design is unusually disciplined for a systems-adjacent behavioral result: frozen contract, fresh container per run, zero judge calls, a mechanically defined tool-command signature, an ID-renaming placebo, and a quotient control that keeps the split representation but collapses semantic duplicates before the same top-k budget. The 6/6 vs 0/6 primary contrast with 3/3 restoration in both controls is internally coherent and passes its own frozen gates. My audit conclusion: this does upgrade STRI from a pure control-plane/specification observation to a bounded downstream behavioral consequence, but the upgrade is narrower than the abstract's framing suggests. The behavioral 'consequence' is the *removal* of a destructive signature by crowding out a cleanup skill; the chain is deterministic at the retrieval step and the behavioral step is a single archived substrate with a single executor, n=6/6/3/3, and a signature whose causal attribution to the missing skill is inferred rather than isolated. The evidence chain is valid as far as it goes; it does not need another experiment to be submittable under the manuscript's stated claim boundary, but it must not be allowed to carry more weight than 'one bounded representation-to-retrieval-to-behavior consequence.'
strengths: The intervention is a true representation intervention: splitting one skill into four exact-semantic IDs changes package bookkeeping while holding executable semantics fixed, which is exactly the STRI nuisance channel rather than a content perturbation.

The retrieval-set crowd-out mechanism is deterministic and directly observable: four clone IDs consume four of five top-k slots, excluding the post-checkout skill. This is a clean, checkable intermediate endpoint rather than an inferred latent mechanism.

The ID-placebo (C) is the right control for the most obvious confound: renaming the identifier without adding multiplicity preserves the semantic retrieval set and restores the signature 3/3, ruling out an ID-token-only or any-change-to-the-prompt explanation at this scale.

The quotient control (D) is the theoretically correct restoration: it keeps the split representation but collapses exact duplicates before the same five-slot budget, restoring both the retrieval set and the signature 3/3. This directly tests the Proposition-1 quotient-factorization mechanism in a behavioral setting, which is the manuscript's core theoretical claim.

Execution hygiene is strong: fresh Codex container per run, frozen prompt, single executor, zero judge calls, zero training steps, mechanically defined outcome read from tool commands, and a hashed run manifest. This removes the most common sources of behavioral-eval contamination.

The outcome is mechanical and pre-specified (post-checkout workflow containing git reset --hard and forced cleanup), not a model-graded or human-graded judgment, which keeps the behavioral endpoint inside the paper's no-judge discipline.

The manuscript's own claim boundary is mostly honest: it explicitly disclaims end-to-end AutoSkill utility, general safety, and population-level effects, and the receipt's authority block mirrors those limits.
weaknesses: The direction of the behavioral effect is the *absence* of a destructive signature in the split condition, not the presence of a measured downstream capability change. The paper's narrative is 'representation alters realized behavior,' but the actual observation is 'representation change removes a cleanup skill and therefore removes a cleanup behavior.' That is a real consequence, but it is a subtractive/crowd-out consequence, not a demonstration that representation distortion changes task performance or induces a new behavior.

Attribution of the signature to the crowding-out of the post-checkout skill is inferred from co-occurrence, not isolated. The split changes the retrieved set from five semantic skills to two; the signature disappearance is ascribed to losing the reset/clean skill, but the experiment does not include a condition that removes only that skill (or adds it back under the split representation) to prove it is the necessary and sufficient retrieved element for the signature.

Sample sizes are small and asymmetric (6/6/3/3). The Fisher p=0.00108 is exact for the 6-vs-0 contrast but the control arms are n=3 each; a single discordant run in C or D would break the frozen gates. The result is fragile to one-run perturbations even though it is internally consistent.

Single substrate, single executor, single frozen prompt, single library. The receipt itself states this is one archived P19 behavioral-harm substrate and does not authorize generalization. The behavioral consequence is therefore an existence proof, not a characterization of when representation sensitivity produces behavioral effects.

The retrieval crowd-out is deterministic given the library and top-k, so the only stochastic link is the executor's behavior conditional on the retrieved set. The experiment does not report executor-level variance, run-to-run command diversity, or whether the signature is an all-or-nothing property of the retrieved set versus a graded response.

The destructive signature is a proxy for 'behavioral consequence' chosen because it is mechanically readable; the packet gives no evidence that this signature is representative of behaviorally meaningful downstream effects rather than an especially legible edge case.

The placebo and quotient controls each restore the signature in 3/3 runs, but the experiment does not include a negative behavioral control (e.g., a retrieval set that includes the post-checkout skill but is otherwise perturbed) to show the signature is specifically tied to that skill's presence rather than to any five-skill retrieval set.
remaining_high_risk: Causal attribution of the signature to the crowded-out post-checkout skill specifically, as opposed to the change in retrieved-set size/composition, is not experimentally isolated.
One-substrate, one-executor, one-prompt fragility: the behavioral consequence could be idiosyncratic to this P19 library and the Doubao executor's reaction to this particular retrieval set.
Small-n control arms (3/3) mean the restoration claims rest on minimal replication; the frozen gates are all-or-nothing and would fail on a single discordant run.

The abstract's phrasing 'removes a mechanical destructive post-checkout signature' risks being read as a safety-relevant behavioral result; the packet supports only a mechanically defined command-signature change on one substrate.

The deterministic retrieval step means the experiment is really testing executor sensitivity to a known retrieval change; it does not test whether representation distortions in general propagate to behavior, only that this one engineered crowd-out does.
claim_boundary_violations: Abstract sentence 'representation can alter realized behavior without semantic change' is defensible only under the bounded reading; the manuscript body mostly respects this, but the abstract does not state that the alteration is the removal of a cleanup behavior via retrieval crowd-out on a single substrate, which is a material narrowing.

The contribution bullet 'AutoSkill provides a controlled one-substrate representation-to-retrieval-to-behavior consequence with ID-placebo and quotient restoration' is accurate; however, the abstract's juxtaposition with the Fisher p-value invites a stronger causal reading than the 6/6/3/3 single-substrate design supports.

No violation of the stated discussion-section boundary was found; the discussion explicitly disclaims utility, regret, and system-wide safety. The risk is abstract-level emphasis, not body-level overreach.
previous_kimi_review.highest_value_next_action: Add one targeted isolation condition before or alongside submission: under the split representation, explicitly re-inject the crowded-out post-checkout skill into the retrieved set (or equivalently remove only that skill from the original five-skill set) and show the signature disappears/appears accordingly. This converts the inferred attribution ('crowd-out of the reset/clean skill causes the signature loss') into a demonstrated necessity/sufficiency claim, and it is cheap because the retrieval seam is already controlled and the container infrastructure exists.
previous_kimi_review.strongest_alternative_explanation: The signature disappearance is not caused by losing the post-checkout reset/clean skill specifically, but by the retrieved set shrinking from five semantic skills to two (or by the dominance of four identical Makefile IDs in the prompt). Under this alternative, any retrieval-set contraction or any four-copy repetition would suppress the signature regardless of which skill is excluded, and the quotient control restores the signature simply because it restores a five-skill set, not because it restores that skill. The current design cannot rule this out because it never varies retrieved-set size/composition independently of the post-checkout skill's presence.
previous_kimi_review.id_placebo_assessment: The ID-placebo is well designed for its stated purpose: it changes only the source identifier without adding multiplicity, preserves the five-semantic-skill retrieval set, and restores the signature 3/3. This adequately rules out an ID-token-only or mere-perturbation explanation at this scale. Its limitation is n=3 and that it does not probe whether the *content* of the renamed ID matters; it is a renaming placebo, not a content placebo. Within the claim boundary it is sufficient.
previous_kimi_review.quotient_control_assessment: The quotient control is the strongest element of the design because it directly instantiates the paper's Proposition-1 mechanism in a behavioral setting: keep the split representation, collapse exact duplicates before the same budget, restore the retrieval set and the signature 3/3. This is exactly the right control to separate representation-budget mechanics from generic prompt change. Its limits are n=3 and that it restores the entire original retrieval set, so it cannot distinguish 'the post-checkout skill is necessary' from 'a five-skill set is necessary.'
previous_kimi_review.single_substrate_limit: The behavioral consequence is established on one archived P19 library, one executor (doubao-seed-2.0-lite), one frozen prompt, and one top-k operationalization. The receipt explicitly disclaims generalization and task-utility authority. This is acceptable as an existence proof but means the result cannot support any claim about how often representation sensitivity propagates to behavior, only that it can in this engineered case. The manuscript body respects this; the abstract should be checked to ensure it does not imply a broader behavioral phenomenon.
previous_kimi_review.what_would_change_view: I would raise the significance assessment from material to large if (a) the isolation condition above showed the post-checkout skill is individually necessary and sufficient for the signature under both original and split representations, and (b) at least one additional independent substrate or executor reproduced the representation->retrieval->behavior chain with the same placebo/quotient discipline. I would lower it to small if it emerged that the signature is an all-or-nothing function of retrieved-set size rather than of the specific crowded-out skill, or if the executor's behavior were shown to be insensitive to retrieval-set composition in control conditions.
previous_kimi_review.manuscript_positioning: Position the AutoSkill result as a bounded existence proof: a single, carefully controlled demonstration that a semantics-preserving representation change can propagate through identity-level retrieval to a mechanically defined executed behavior, with placebo and quotient restoration. Keep it out of the abstract's causal headline unless the abstract also states the direction (removal of a cleanup behavior via crowd-out) and the single-substrate scope. Do not let it carry the paper's significance; the theoretical characterization and the released-system geometry remain the core contributions, with AutoSkill as corroborating behavioral evidence.
evidence_blockers: No isolation condition varying the post-checkout skill's presence independently of retrieved-set size/composition.
No executor-variance or command-diversity reporting to show the behavioral step is robust rather than a single brittle reaction.
Control arms at n=3 with all-or-nothing frozen gates, so the restoration claim is minimally replicated.
No second substrate or executor to bound substrate specificity.
